options.systemPromptTemplate: You are a restaurant health-code compliance analyst reviewing a single health department inspection note for one quick-service restaurant (QSR) location. Extract structured fields as strict JSON with EXACTLY the requested keys and no others. Base severity strictly on the food-safety risk described, not on tone. critical = imminent health hazard requiring immediate correction (e.g. temperature abuse, pest infestation, sewage backup); major = significant violation requiring prompt correction (e.g. equipment malfunction, missing documentation with real risk); minor = low-risk housekeeping or paperwork issue. Output valid JSON only.

attributes.name: violation_category
attributes.description: Category of health-code violation observed: Temperature Control, Pest Control, Cross-Contamination, Handwashing/Hygiene, Sanitation, Employee Certification, or Facility Maintenance

attributes.name: severity
attributes.description: Violation severity — must be exactly one of: 'critical', 'major', or 'minor', judged strictly on food-safety risk described in the note

attributes.name: code_section
attributes.description: Best-effort FDA Food Code or local health-code section reference for this violation, e.g. '3-501.16' for hot holding temperature

attributes.name: recommended_corrective_action
attributes.description: One concise, specific, actionable corrective step the location manager should take to fix this violation

parameters.content:
## Multi-Location QSR Health Inspection Corrective-Action Fan-Out & Compliance Digest

### How it works
Start the daily sweep, split the inspection array, normalize each location, and process one location per loop iteration.  Extract severity, calculate the configured corrective deadline, and append the location log.  After the loop completes, compute the regional risk score, append the summary, and check the escalation threshold. Send an escalation when the threshold is met or mark no escalation. 

### Setup
1. Connect the credentials required by the integration nodes and select the correct account for each service.
2. Replace all placeholder endpoints, recipients, chat IDs, table names and document IDs with your own values.
3. Confirm that incoming fields match the expressions and that every destination accepts the mapped output fields.
4. Run the workflow manually with representative sample data. Test every decision branch and inspect each external action.
5. Review retry and error behavior before enabling the trigger. Keep this feedback copy inactive until setup and testing are complete.

### Customization
Adjust schedules, thresholds, prompts and notification destinations to match your process. Keep the documented input and output contract aligned with any changes.

## Prepare the inspection batch

Start the daily sweep, split the inspection array, normalize each location, and process one location per loop iteration.

## Score each location

Extract severity, calculate the configured corrective deadline, and append the location log.

## Calculate the daily summary

After the loop completes, compute the regional risk score, append the summary, and check the escalation threshold.

## Send the daily notifications

Send an escalation when the threshold is met or mark no escalation.
